_meta._mapper_provenance: stated in intake; flagged as needs-verification in prior review
_meta.fit_summary: Breaks the schema HARD. Top Gun is not a navigable-space game; it is a mission state-machine + precision skill-checks. Two load-bearing contracts (World Graph #3, Room/Tile #8) are semantically inapplicable. Compare to RCR (~70% fit).
contracts_inapplicable: world_graph_contract  -> no navigable space; forced into degenerate linear chain (kept only to demonstrate the break)
ability_system_contract  -> no progression abilities; closest analog is pre-mission loadout, moved to loadout_contract
room_tile_contract  -> no spatial layout; repurposed as view-mode states, which is not what the contract is for
extensions_beyond_spec: mission_script_contract  (the CORRECT representation of structure; replaces world_graph for non-spatial games)
precision_sequence_contract  (carrier landing + refueling skill-checks -- the DEFINING mechanic, no home in the 9)
instrument_telemetry_contract  (speed/altitude/heading/lock as a live game-state display layer)

canonical_known: carrier landing as defining skill gate
needs_rom_extraction: exact landing/refuel tolerance windows and frame data

open_measure_flags: mission order modeled as MiG -> carrier -> fortress -> satellite; confirm count and sequence
missile types modeled as A/B/C with relative tradeoffs; exact values unknown
whether refuel is per-mission or only between certain missions is unconfirmed

input_contract.core_ability_style: instrument management + missile loadout strategy + precision landing
input_contract._strain: core_ability_style has no clean home -- it is skill-check + resource-management, not the movement/combat ability style the field expects

interpretation_layer._movement_model_note: FIRST USE of the 'aerial' enum value across both intakes -- but the player_controller below proves the contract has no aerial *implementation*
interpretation_layer._world_structure_strain: STRAIN: enum was (dense | vertical | sprawling) -- all spatial. Top Gun is 'scripted', a value the enum does not contain. Structure is a mission timeline, not a space.
interpretation_layer._progression_style_strain: STRAIN: enum was (ability-gated | key-based | hybrid). None apply. Progression is linear mission completion + landing skill gates.
interpretation_layer._risk_profile_note: real risk is fuel depletion + failed landing, not enemy damage

world_graph_contract._INAPPLICABLE: Top Gun has no navigable space. The nodes below are a DEGENERATE LINEAR CHAIN kept only to show the break. Edges are scripted transitions, not traversable connections. The correct representation lives in mission_script_contract.

ability_system_contract._INAPPLICABLE: No progression abilities. The only player-chosen capability is missile loadout, which is a strategic resource selection, not a path-gating ability. Moved to loadout_contract.

player_controller_contract._strain: MAJOR. The movement block is platformer-shaped (speed/jump_force/gravity/air_control) and is almost entirely wrong for flight. Below is the correct aerial/instrument model the contract does NOT define. All values tier=estimated.

movement_DEPRECATED_FIELDS._note: these fields are meaningless in a cockpit flight model

player_controller_contract._iframes_note: no i-frames; survivability is governed by fuel + collision, not hit-stun

enemy_system_contract._note: loosest-fitting clean contract. STRAIN: spawn_nodes points at the degenerate mission chain; real spawns are script-driven waves. health tier=estimated.

boss_contract._strain: Fortress / satellite base modeled as boss-style objective targets. The multi-phase pattern model over-specifies; these are high-durability destruction objectives, and reward is mission-advance, not an ability.

room_tile_contract._INAPPLICABLE: No spatial layout exists. There is a static cockpit mask + a moving horizon, not authored rooms. Repurposed below as VIEW-MODE STATES, which is not what this contract is for -- it confirms the genre has no tile/layout layer.

mission_script_contract._extension: EXTENSION. The CORRECT replacement for world_graph in a non-spatial game. Structure is a linear ordered timeline of objectives and skill-checks.

loadout_contract._extension: EXTENSION. Pre-mission strategic capability selection -- the thing ability_system_contract tried and failed to represent.
loadout_contract._note: exact stats tier=needs_rom_extraction; relative tradeoffs are the design-critical part

precision_sequence_contract._extension: EXTENSION -- and the single most important one. The carrier landing and refueling are the DEFINING mechanic and have NO home anywhere in the original 9. These are discrete skill-checks with tolerance windows, not combat and not traversal.

landing._note: this is what players remember Top Gun for; tolerance is deliberately punishing

resource_contract._extension: EXTENSION. Fuel is a depleting survival resource -- distinct from RCR's accumulating money economy. (Both genres need a resource layer the 9 never had; they need it in opposite directions.)

instrument_telemetry_contract._extension: EXTENSION. Live game-state read out to the player as instruments. In a metroidvania this is a simple HUD; here it IS the gameplay surface (you fly the numbers, not the plane).
instrument_telemetry_contract.readability_priority: instruments must stay legible against sky/ocean contrast
instrument_telemetry_contract._note: overlaps the pixel/rendering MCP -- readability is a rendering constraint, but the values are game state

checks: mission_sequence_complete: every step reachable in order to terminal landing
loadout_sufficiency: at least one loadout can clear each combat mission's objective quota
fuel_budget: fuel at mission start is enough to reach a refuel/landing before depletion
skill_check_achievable: tolerance windows are non-empty and physically reachable by the flight_model
validation_layer._strain: The original spatial checks (reachability, gate-solvability, dead-ends) are inapplicable -- there is no space to traverse. ALL meaningful checks here are new: fuel_budget and skill_check_achievable have no analog in the Controidvania-derived validator.
